title: Telemetry Cost, Fidelity, and SLO Governance Playbook
author: Asha Narayanan
body:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood's approach to governing telemetry fidelity and ingest cost while ensuring SLO integrity and predictable capacity planning. It codifies decisions for sampling, retention, synthetic traffic, and tooling controls necessary to keep observability economically sustainable without degrading incident response or SLO observability.

Audience
- SREs, platform engineers, and service owners responsible for SLOs, capacity planning, and observability budgets.
- Product and security stakeholders who need cost or compliance inputs for telemetry policy changes.

Goals
- Keep observability costs within target budget (Finance tag: OBSERV-plat) while retaining necessary fidelity for SLOs and RCA.
- Provide a reproducible decision workflow for changing sampling, retention, or synthetic traffic.
- Ensure telemetry configuration changes are safe, reversible, and traceable.

Principles
1) SLO-first: Any telemetry policy must preserve the ability to compute SLOs and detect SLO violations with >=95% fidelity at the alerting window.
2) Tiered fidelity: Higher criticality services (P0/P1) get full-fidelity traces/metrics; lower tiers may use sampling, aggregation, or longer scrape intervals.
3) Cost-as-a-first-class signal: Ingest and storage budgets are tracked monthly and tied to error-budget policy changes.
4) Automation and auditability: All telemetry tuning must be made via CI or an automated change path with audit logs.

Definitions
- Fidelity: degree to which raw telemetry (traces, logs, metrics) is preserved.
- Ingest cost: recurring cost attributable to telemetry senders (agent/SDK) and collector/ingestion pipeline.
- SLO fidelity budget: minimum telemetry coverage required to compute, alert, and investigate SLOs.

Service Classification and Telemetry Baselines
- Table: Service tier -> Minimum telemetry set -> Retention -> Max monthly ingest budget

| Service Tier | Minimum telemetry set | Retention (metrics/traces/logs) | Max ingest budget % of product budget |
|--------------|----------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Critical (P0) | Metrics (1s), Traces (100%), Error logs (100%) | 90d/30d/180d | 35% |
| Important (P1) | Metrics (10s), Traces (10%), Error logs (50%) | 30d/14d/90d | 20% |
| Standard (P2) | Metrics (30s), Traces (1%), Error logs (20%) | 14d/7d/30d | 10% |
| Low (P3) | Metrics (60s), Traces (0%), Aggregated logs | 7d/0/7d | 3% |

Note: budgets are guidance; finance approvals required for changes >10% deviance.

Telemetry Controls and Recipes
- Sampling: Prefer adaptive tail-based sampling for traces and head-based sampling only for extremely high-throughput callers. Use the following guardrails:
  1. MinTraceRetentionForSLO: ensure at least 100 unique traces per alerting window for a given operation.
  2. MinErrorTraceCapture: capture 100% of error-tagged spans (errors, status>=500) regardless of sampling.
- Aggregation: For metrics with large cardinality (user_id, session_id), apply rollup metrics (count_by_status, p50/p95 latency buckets) at the SDK/agent before ingestion.
- Dynamic sampling policy: scale sampling rates down linearly when monthly ingest approaches budget threshold 70% and trigger review at 90%.

Sampling configuration examples (YAML)
- Example: head-sampler config for a high-volume service (apply via telemetry-config repo):

  sampling_policy: 
    default_rate: 0.01
    error_rate: 1.0
    rules:
      - match: 'http.path startsWith "/api/critical"'
        rate: 1.0
      - match: 'http.status >= 500'
        rate: 1.0

CLI snippets
- To view current ingest rates (Grafana / Prometheus query via CLI):
  curl -sS "${GRAFANA_API}/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=telemetry_ingest_bytes_total%7Bservice=\"svc-name\"%7D" | jq
- To update sampling rate in the config repo (example):
  git clone git@github.com:redwood/telemetry-config.git
  sed -i 's/default_rate: 0.02/default_rate: 0.01/' svc-name/sampling.yaml
  git commit -am "reduce sampling for svc-name to 1% to reduce ingest" && git push && open-pr

SLO and Error Budget Mapping
- For every SLO, the owning service must declare a Telemetry Requirements block with:
  - SLO id and window (e.g., request_success_rate / 30d / p99 latency alerting window),
  - Required metrics and trace coverage (percent traces and minimum error traces),
  - Acceptable telemetry degradation mode (what metadata may be dropped before SLO observability is impacted).

Example SLO Telemetry Requirement (text):
- SLO: api_success_rate_v1 (99.95% over 30d)
  - Required metrics: request_count, success_count, latency_p95
  - Required trace coverage: 5% sampling of successful requests, 100% of error traces
  - RCA requirement: on SLO breach, team must be able to find 10 error traces and request-level logs for 75% of breached requests within retention period.

Error Budget Governance (when to change telemetry)
- If a service consumes >70% of its telemetry ingest budget, the SRE owner must:
  1) Notify finance and platform (automated alert).
  2) Run quick triage: verify cardinality explosion, unbounded label dimensions, or change in traffic.
  3) Apply temporary sampling throttle (5–15% safe range) targeting non-error paths and monitor SLO impact for 48h.
  4) If sampling throttle persists beyond 7 days, open a telemetry-cost remediation epic and schedule capacity/cost review.
- If the service has an SLO on the verge of burning error budget and telemetry reduction would affect SLO observability, prioritize SLO preservation (reduce retention of non-essential logs, not traces).

Capacity Planning Interfaces
- Telemetry is an input to capacity planning (RPS, p95 latency, queue depths). To avoid circularity, capacity planners must:
  - Use synthetic load and sampling-corrected metrics to estimate true RPS when sampling <100%.
  - Maintain a mapping file: sampling_rate -> correction_factor for each metric. This file is stored in the infra/capacity repo.

Operational Tooling Requirements
- Collector configuration must support:
  - Dynamic sampling changes without restart (hot reload),
  - Per-service rate limiting and burst protection,
  - Per-tenant tagging for billing and quota enforcement.
- Metric ingestion pipeline must export: daily ingest bytes per service, per-data-type (metrics/traces/logs), and per-tenant cost attribution.

Runbook excerpts (for telemetry incidents)
1) Incident: sudden telemetry ingest spike (alerts: telemetry_ingest_bytes_total > 2x baseline for 30m)
   - Owner: telemetry-oncall (pager-duty)
   - Steps:
     a) Acknowledge alert and open incident in Incident Board template.
     b) Query top-k services by ingest: Grafana dashboard -> Top ingest by service panel.
     c) Check recent deploys for those services (CI/CD deploy history) and rollback if correlated.
     d) Check for cardinality increase (new label, tracing header misuse) via:
        curl "${GRAFANA_API}/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=count by(label)(telemetry_label_cardinality_total)" | jq
     e) If root cause is unbounded cardinality, apply immediate label-drop rule in collector with scope: service=<svc> and monitor ingest for 15m.
     f) If root cause is traffic spike, apply temporary per-service throttle: collectorsctl set-rate svc <svc> 50MB/s
     g) Communicate to owners and Finance about potential budget impact; file follow-up.

2) Incident: SLO alert but low trace coverage
   - Owner: service-oncall
   - Steps:
     a) Confirm SLO alert via SLO dashboard.
     b) Check current sampling rate and error-trace capture rule for the service.
     c) If sampling < required threshold, temporarily raise sampler for matching endpoints (hot reload).
     d) If cause is collector-side drop, escalate to telemetry-infra and enable bypass for errors.
     e) Once root cause fixed, document in post-incident review and restore planned sampling.

Decision and Change Process
- Telemetry changes follow the same policy as infra config changes: PR -> automated tests (ingest regression test, SLO signal test) -> staged rollout -> audit log entry.
- For any change that reduces trace coverage for a critical SLO, require in_review status and sign-off from SRE manager and product owner.

Metrics and Dashboards to Maintain
- Ingest: daily_ingest_bytes{service}, pct_of_budget{service}, retention_cost_estimate{service}
- Fidelity: trace_capture_rate{service,operation}, errors_captured_pct{service}
- SLO observability: slo_signal_integrity{service,slo_id} (boolean indicating whether required metrics/traces are present for the alerting window)

Post-incident and Reliability Initiatives
- Every incident involving telemetry fidelity or cost must include the following in the PIR:
  - Timeline showing telemetry ingest and sampling changes,
  - Effect on SLO detection latency and RCA time,
  - Root cause analysis including any unbounded cardinality patterns,
  - Concrete remediation: label suppression, SDK hygiene change, or retention/tiering plan.
- Quarterly reliability initiative: Telemetry Health Sprint
  - Goals: reduce unnecessary trace rate by 30%, implement adaptive tail-based sampling in top-10 ingesters, and automate budget alerts per service.
  - Deliverables: sampling-policy library, automated cost annotation in PRs, and a telemetry-cost dashboard with owners.

Ownership and Contacts
- Telemetry platform: telemetry-infra@redwood.com (primary), Slack: #telemetry-platform
- Capacity planning: capacity-sre@redwood.com, Kane Park (capacity lead)
- Finance contact for observability spend: observability-finance@redwood.com

Appendices
- Appendix A: Example Prometheus recording rule to correct for sampling (pseudocode)
  - record: svc_requests_total_corrected
    expr: svc_requests_total_observed / scalar(sampling_rate)

- Appendix B: Audit checklist before changing sampling
  1. Confirm SLO telemetry requirements documented and owners notified.
  2. Run ingest simulation and cost projection.
  3. Validate automated rollback and set alert at 70% of budget impact.
